shifts.summary: Candidates reported the exam overall as moderate in difficulty. Reasoning was seen as ranging from easy to difficult, while GA was mostly moderate. Quant was generally difficult, and English varied between easy and moderate. Good attempts varied by section but most candidates attempted 15–23 questions well.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 10 October 2026 was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 has been reported as moderate overall, with good attempts ranging between 75 and 82 percent across sections. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending analysis and will be updated once sufficient candidate feedback is collected. All figures presented are unofficial, and SSC normally normalises scores across shifts to ensure fairness.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates who appeared in shift 1 on 10 October 2026 described the exam as moderate in overall difficulty. The other two shifts have not yet been analysed, so their overall difficulty will be reported later.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were recorded for shift 1 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: For shift 1 on 10 October 2026, good attempts were reported to be between 75 % and 82 % overall, with most candidates attempting 15–23 questions well across sections.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for shifts 2 and 3 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026 be available?
faqs.a: The analysis for shifts 2 and 3 will be added a few hours after each shift ends, once enough candidate reviews are collected.

faqs.q: Are the figures reported for shift 1 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No. The figures are unofficial and based on candidate feedback; official statistics will be released by SSC later.

faqs.q: Does SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure that candidates are evaluated on a comparable basis regardless of the shift they attended.
